author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects schtasks creating the task names that the MS SQL Server brute-force toolkit uses for persistence:
MicrosoftEdgeUpdateTaskMachineUA and MicrosoftEdgeUpdateTaskMachineCore with fixed GUIDs, and Microsoft_UPDATES.
The real Edge updater uses different GUIDs per install.
false_positives: Unknown
name: Scheduled Task Disguised as Microsoft Edge Update in the SQL Server Toolkit
query: process.executable.caseless:*\\schtasks.exe AND (process.command_line:(*CEC15D9B\-F4BB\-446A\-B6E1\-C61E74B016A2* OR *4C33CE3F\-7722\-4257\-AF83\-351A4911C159* OR *Microsoft_UPDATES*))

author: ThreatDefence
description: A web server, runtime or database process started a shell, download tool or netcat. ARTEX agents explore a host this way after exploiting a web application.
name: Web or Database Service Spawns a Shell or Download Tool
query:
process where event.type == "start" and
  process.parent.name in ("nginx", "httpd", "apache2", "php-fpm", "java", "node", "mysqld", "mariadbd", "postgres",
                          "w3wp.exe", "httpd.exe", "java.exe", "node.exe", "php-cgi.exe", "sqlservr.exe", "mysqld.exe") and
  process.name in ("sh", "bash", "dash", "curl", "wget", "nc", "ncat", "socat", "busybox",
                   "cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "curl.exe", "certutil.exe", "bitsadmin.exe")

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects RedAmon's self-naming user agents (RedAmon-AISurfaceRecon/1.0, RedAmon-CachePoison/1.0 and the
"compatible; RedAmon" strings), the XSS canary rEdAm0n1337XsS its agent is told to use in every parameter, and the
rdmncb cache buster of its cache poisoning tests. All are defaults of the published code.
false_positives: Authorized tests with RedAmon
name: RedAmon User Agent or Canary in Web Logs
query: user_agent.original:*RedAmon* OR (url.query:(*rEdAm0n1337XsS* OR *rdmncb\=cb*)) OR cs-referer:*rEdAm0n1337XsS*

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects the X-ARTX-KEY request header and ARTEX probe marker strings in requests. Community-
reported, so treat a match as a lead and confirm with other activity from the same source.
false_positives: Authorized penetration tests that use ARTEX
name: ARTEX Probe Marker in HTTP Request
query: (url.query:(*ARTEX_WRITE_PROBE* OR *ARTX_PERSIST_OK* OR *artex_control_marker_zz9q* OR *ARTEX\-PROBE\-* OR *artex\-probe\-*)) OR cs-headers:*X\-ARTX\-KEY*

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects requests to the WSUS administration, reporting or server-sync web services. JPCERT/CC Case E reports attacks
on internet-facing WSUS servers by operators using Cairn, CyberStrikeAI and ARTEX. These services should not answer
the internet; client endpoints are excluded.
false_positives: Internal WSUS administration consoles and downstream servers reaching the log source
name: WSUS Administration or Sync API Requested
query: url.path:(*\/ApiRemoting30\/WebService.asmx* OR *\/ServerSyncWebService\/ServerSyncWebService.asmx* OR *\/ReportingWebService\/ReportingWebService.asmx*)

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects files attackers write into Hermes Agent's home folder: the godmode jailbreak prefill file and skill folder, the
loot folder Carbonato's GH0ST persona fills with stolen keys, and Carbonato's persistence files.
false_positives: Researchers installing Hermes optional security skills
name: Hermes Agent Jailbreak, Loot or Carbonato Files Written
query: (TargetFilename:(*\/.hermes\/loot\/* OR *\/.hermes\/skills\/security\/godmode\/*)) OR TargetFilename:*\/.hermes\/prefill.json OR (TargetFilename:\/opt\/gh0st\/* OR (TargetFilename:(\/usr\/local\/bin\/.docker\-network\-monitor OR \/usr\/sbin\/systemd\-logind)))

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects DNS lookups of strix.gateway.scarf.sh, which Strix calls at the start and end of every scan and for every
finding unless STRIX_TELEMETRY is turned off.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Strix
name: Strix Telemetry DNS Query
query: dns.question.name:(strix.gateway.scarf.sh OR *.strix.gateway.scarf.sh)

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects Pentest Swarm AI writing its consent file and log under the user's home folder. authorization.log gets one
JSON line for every real target (time, target, scope, method, user), so it is also the first file to read on a host
where the tool was found.
false_positives: Penetration testers running Pentest Swarm AI
name: Pentest Swarm AI Authorization Record Written
query: TargetFilename:(*\/.pentestswarm\/authorization.* OR *\\.pentestswarm\\authorization.*)

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects Xalgorix running: the binary or its container image, and the shell wrapper it puts in front of every
command the agent runs (export XALGORIX_WORKSPACE=..., the __xalgorix_resolve_path function, and xalgorix-scan-init
when it runs as root). Xalgorix is an autonomous penetration testing agent that needs no approval for tool calls.
false_positives: Bug bounty hunters and security teams running Xalgorix
name: Xalgorix Agent on a Host
query: process.executable:*\/xalgorix OR (process.command_line:(*XALGORIX_WORKSPACE\=* OR *__xalgorix_resolve_path* OR *xalgorix\-scan\-init* OR *xalgord\/xalgorix* OR *xalgorix\ \-\-web*))

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects outbound or reverse-proxy requests whose user agent names the ARTEX framework or its renamed
builds. Outbound hits mean a host on your network is running ARTEX.
false_positives: Authorized penetration tests that use ARTEX
name: ARTEX Agentic Attack Framework User Agent in Proxy Logs
query: user_agent.original:(*artex\-readonly\/* OR *artex\-pentest\/* OR *artex\-audit\/* OR *artex\-verify\/* OR *artex\-spawn\/* OR *ARTEX\-worker\/* OR *artex\-enrich\/* OR *artex\-i21861\-canary* OR *artex\-agent* OR *artex\-judge\-* OR *ARTeX\-authorized\-pentest* OR *Mozilla\/5.0\ ARTeX* OR *Mozilla\/5.0\ \(ARTEX\)* OR *ArtExVerify\/* OR *ArtEx\/1.0* OR *scopeweaver* OR *spa\-api\-recon*)

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description: Detects the HexStrike tool server, its MCP client, and tools started by the server.
false_positives: Authorized red team use of HexStrike
name: HexStrike Server or MCP Client Process
query: (process.command_line:(*hexstrike_server.py* OR *hexstrike_mcp.py*)) OR process.parent.command_line:*hexstrike_server.py*

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects a certificate or secret added to an application or service principal. Storm-0940 used
compromised applications to add credentials to other applications and assign themselves roles.
Review who or what made the change: an application changing another application is the case to
chase.
false_positives: Administrators rotating application secrets
name: Credential Added to an Entra ID Application
query: properties.message:("Update application \- Certificates and secrets management" OR "Add service principal credentials")

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects the CyberStrikeAI implant's Linux cron persistence, (crontab -l; echo '@reboot <implant> &') | sort -u | crontab -,
and its curl_beacon one-liner, a bash loop that POSTs to /check_in with an X-Implant-Token header every 5 seconds.
false_positives: Administrators adding @reboot jobs the same way (cron selection only)
name: CyberStrikeAI Implant Linux Persistence or curl Beacon
query: (process.command_line:*@reboot* AND process.command_line:*sort\ \-u\ \|\ crontab\ \-*) OR process.command_line:*X\-Implant\-Token*

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects the LaunchAgent the CyberStrikeAI implant writes on macOS, ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.apple.systemupdate.plist,
with RunAtLoad and KeepAlive. Apple does not ship a per-user agent with this label.
false_positives: Unknown
name: CyberStrikeAI Implant LaunchAgent com.apple.systemupdate
query: TargetFilename:*\/Library\/LaunchAgents\/com.apple.systemupdate.plist

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects files Cairn writes on a worker host: graph.yaml task snapshots under /tmp/cairn-prompts/, the Pi worker's
models.json with the provider API key under /tmp/cairn-pi/, and the tsec-actions skill from the Tencent TCH
competition setup that operators' worker images still carry.
false_positives: Authorized red team use of Cairn
name: Cairn Task Snapshot, Pi Provider Key or Competition Skill Written
query: TargetFilename:(*\/tmp\/cairn\-prompts\/* OR *\/tmp\/cairn\-pi\/* OR *\/skills\/tsec\-actions\/SKILL.md*)

author: ThreatDefence
description: Placeholder probe paths, alg none JWTs or the fixed OAuth callback probe that ARTEX sends while mapping a web application.
name: ARTEX Web Probe Artifacts
query: url.original : (*zzz-nonexistent-xyz123* or *zzz_nonexistent_abc.txt* or *Notexist-xyz* or *eyJhbGciOiJub25lI* or *eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJub25lI* or *eyJhbGciOiJOb25lI* or *eyJhbGciOiJOT05FI* or *code=AAAA&state=notvalidb64!!*)

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects the Agent Zero image being run, its UI starting inside the container, and its tunnel server that publishes the
UI to the internet. Agent Zero ships a hacker profile on a Kali base; GTIG reported threat-actor experimentation with it.
false_positives: Developers and researchers running Agent Zero
name: Agent Zero Container, UI or Tunnel Started
query: process.command_line:(*agent0ai\/agent\-zero* OR *self_update_manager.py\ docker\-run\-ui* OR *\/a0\/run_tunnel.py*)

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects the page readers of AI agent CLIs: Qwen Code, Kimi CLI, opencode and Claude Code (which Cairn's workers
run with DeepSeek behind it). Agents read target pages with these while curl, Python and Kali tools do the rest.
Ordinary users send the same strings, so treat a hit as context and correlate with scanning from the same address.
false_positives: Developers and users of these agents reading public pages
name: AI Agent Page Reader User Agent in Web Server Logs
query: user_agent.original:*Claude\-User\ \(claude\-code\/* OR (user_agent.original:(QwenCode\/* OR KimiCLI\/* OR opencode\/*))

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects command lines that only Cairn produces: the Codex worker's model_provider="cairn" override, the Pi worker's
--provider cairn and /tmp/cairn-pi/ agent folder, the dispatcher and server entry points, and the cairn-dispatch-
worker containers.
false_positives: Authorized red team use of Cairn
name: Cairn Agent Worker or Dispatcher Command Line
query: process.command_line:(*model_provider\=\"cairn\"* OR *model_providers.cairn.base_url* OR *\-\-provider\ cairn* OR *\/tmp\/cairn\-pi\/* OR *\/tmp\/cairn\-prompts\/* OR *cairn\ dispatch\ \-\-config* OR *cairn\-dispatch\-* OR *cairn\-worker\-container*)

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description: Detects requests to PentAGI's update endpoint or to console API paths that only PentAGI uses.
false_positives: Approved PentAGI deployments
name: PentAGI Console API Requested Through a Proxy
query: url.original:*\/api\/v1\/proxy\/updates\/pentagi\/check* OR url.domain:update.pentagi.com

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects FilterLogEvents calls whose filter pattern searches for passwords or AWS access keys.
Datadog saw a stolen key search CloudWatch logs with patterns such as ?password ?AKIA, always with a
limit of 1000.
false_positives: Engineers searching logs for leaked secrets during a cleanup
name: CloudWatch Logs Searched for Secrets
query: (eventSource:logs.amazonaws.com AND eventName:FilterLogEvents) AND (requestParameters.filterPattern:(*password* OR *AKIA* OR *secret* OR *token*))

author: ThreatDefence
description: A process or file carries the names ARTEX agents give their own test artifacts.
name: ARTEX Artifact Names on a Host
query:
any where
  (event.category == "process" and process.command_line : ("*artex-probe-*", "*ArtexProbe*", "*artx5v*", "*art18-*", "*ARTEX_WRITE_PROBE*", "*ARTX_PERSIST_OK*")) or
  (event.category == "file" and (file.name : "artex-probe-*" or file.path : "*ProgramData*artx5v*" or
     file.name in ("cl1217.jsp", "f1219a.jsp", "z1219.jsp", "zzartx0000.php")))

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects lookups of update.pentagi.com and support.pentagi.com. Every PentAGI installation checks for updates every
three hours by default, so a hit shows where PentAGI runs.
false_positives: Approved PentAGI deployments
name: DNS Query for the PentAGI Update Service
query: dns.question.name:(update.pentagi.com OR support.pentagi.com)

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description: Detects HexStrike's hard-coded user agents and the <hexstrikeXSSTest123> reflection probe its browser agent submits.
false_positives: Authorized tests with HexStrike
name: HexStrike User Agent or XSS Probe in Web Logs
query: (user_agent.original:(*HexStrike\-HTTP\-Framework\/* OR *HexStrike\-BrowserAgent\/* OR *Mozilla\/5.0\ \(Compatible\ Exploit\)*)) OR url.query:*hexstrikeXSSTest123*

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects Carbonato's escape from a privileged container into the host (nsenter -t 1 -m -u -n -i), its worm container
names and image, and its persistence paths. Carbonato installs Hermes Agent with a GH0ST persona on each host.
false_positives: Node maintenance scripts that enter the host namespaces and download or schedule something
name: Carbonato Docker Worm Host Escape or Persistence
query: ((process.command_line:*nsenter* AND process.command_line:*\-t\ 1* AND process.command_line:*\-m\ \-u\ \-n\ \-i*) AND (process.command_line:(*curl\ * OR *wget\ * OR *crontab* OR *chattr* OR *authorized_keys* OR *systemctl\ enable* OR *rc.local* OR *.hermes*))) OR (process.command_line:(*netns\-probe* OR *system\/resolved* OR *.docker\-network\-monitor* OR *\/opt\/gh0st\/* OR *CARBONATO_API_KEY*)) OR process.executable:\/usr\/sbin\/systemd\-logind

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description: Detects Okta events whose raw user agent names ARTEX.
false_positives: Authorized penetration tests that use ARTEX
name: ARTEX User Agent in Okta System Log
query: client.userAgent.rawUserAgent:(*artex\-readonly\/* OR *artex\-pentest\/* OR *artex\-audit\/* OR *artex\-verify\/* OR *artex\-spawn\/* OR *ARTEX\-worker\/* OR *artex\-enrich\/* OR *artex\-i21861\-canary* OR *artex\-agent* OR *artex\-judge\-* OR *ARTeX\-authorized\-pentest* OR *Mozilla\/5.0\ ARTeX* OR *Mozilla\/5.0\ \(ARTEX\)* OR *ArtExVerify\/* OR *ArtEx\/1.0* OR *scopeweaver* OR *spa\-api\-recon*)

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects an app role or directory role assigned to a service principal. ARTEX agents in the
Storm-0940 campaign had compromised applications grant themselves roles. Investigate when the
initiator is the same service principal that receives the role.
false_positives: Administrators granting application permissions
name: App Role or Directory Role Assigned to a Service Principal
query: properties.message:("Add app role assignment to service principal" OR "Add member to role")

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects sqlservr.exe starting cmd.exe or PowerShell, the result of xp_cmdshell. The SQL Server toolkit seen in
ARTEX operations enables xp_cmdshell after brute-forcing the sa login, then downloads its loader.
false_positives: Database jobs that use xp_cmdshell by design. Baseline per server
name: SQL Server Spawns a Shell Through xp_cmdshell
query: process.parent.executable.caseless:*\\sqlservr.exe AND (process.executable.caseless:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\bitsadmin.exe))

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects an image pushed to a container registry under a repository named after an attack agent or a write test:
artex-i<issue id>, hermes-h<id>-writecheck, csai-push-probe, xalgorix-pwn, the gh0st/ and fsociety/ namespaces, or
names that hold writecheck, push-probe or pwned. Agents that find a registry open to pushes prove it by pushing a
small image, and they name it after themselves. Open registries on the internet carry these names by the hundred.
A push can be followed by a poisoned copy of one of your own images, so check what else that source pushed.
false_positives: Security teams testing their own registry
A project of your own with one of these words in its name
name: Attack Agent Write Test on a Container Registry
query: (cs-method:PUT AND url.path:\/v2\/* AND url.path:*\/manifests\/*) AND ((url.path:(*writecheck* OR *write\-check* OR *push\-probe* OR *push\-poc* OR *push\-test* OR *pwned* OR *hijack\-canary* OR *regscan\-probe* OR *probe\-write\-test* OR *\/gh0st\/* OR *\/gh0st\-* OR *\/fsociety\/* OR *\/csai\-* OR *\/cyberstrike\-probe* OR *\/xalgorix\-*)) OR url.path:/\/(artex[-_](i\d|probe|push|poc|rce|test|exploit|retest)|ptx-i\d|hermes-h\d)/)

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects a Run value named SystemUpdate, which the CyberStrikeAI implant writes under
HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run to start at logon.
false_positives: Software that really names its Run value SystemUpdate
name: CyberStrikeAI Implant Run Key Value SystemUpdate
query: registry.path:*\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\SystemUpdate

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects Hermes Agent started with approvals switched off (--yolo, HERMES_YOLO_MODE) and the scripts of its bundled
godmode jailbreak skill. Attackers ran Hermes this way against Thailand's Ministry of Finance (Hunt.io) and with
godmode on DeepSeek (Unit 42).
false_positives: Developers running Hermes unattended in a sandbox
Red teams testing model guardrails
name: Hermes Agent With Approvals Off or Its Jailbreak Skill
query: (process.command_line:/(^|[\/\\\s])hermes(\.exe)?(\s|$)|hermes_cli|run_agent\.py|\/\.hermes\// AND (process.command_line:(*\-\-yolo* OR *HERMES_YOLO_MODE*))) OR (process.command_line:(*load_godmode.py* OR *auto_jailbreak.py* OR *parseltongue.py* OR *godmode_race.py*))

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects lookups for request-collection and DNS callback services. ARTEX agents posted command output
to webhook.site across hundreds of rotating URLs. These services are legitimate, so scope the rule
to servers, where they have no business purpose.
false_positives: Developers testing webhooks from workstations. Scope to servers
name: DNS Query to Request Collection or DNS Callback Services
query: dns.question.name:webhook.site OR (dns.question.name:(*.webhook.site OR *.dnslog.cn OR *.interact.sh OR *.oast.fun OR *.requestcatcher.com OR *.pipedream.net))

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects lookups of out-of-band callback services (interactsh oast.* servers, Burp Collaborator, dnslog.cn and others).
Agents such as Strix use them to confirm blind injection, SSRF and XXE. From a server, a hit means a payload ran there.
false_positives: Authorized penetration tests and bug bounty research against your servers
Security engineers testing interactsh or Burp from workstations
name: DNS Query for an Out-of-Band Testing Domain
query: (dns.question.name:(*.oast.fun OR *.oast.pro OR *.oast.live OR *.oast.site OR *.oast.online OR *.oast.me OR *.interact.sh OR *.oastify.com OR *.burpcollaborator.net OR *.dnslog.cn OR *.ceye.io OR *.requestrepo.com OR *.oast.fun. OR *.oast.pro. OR *.oast.live. OR *.oast.site. OR *.oast.online. OR *.oast.me. OR *.interact.sh. OR *.oastify.com. OR *.burpcollaborator.net. OR *.dnslog.cn. OR *.ceye.io. OR *.requestrepo.com.)) AND (NOT (dns.question.name:(polling.oastify.com OR polling.oastify.com. OR polling.burpcollaborator.net OR polling.burpcollaborator.net.)))

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects IIS, Apache, Tomcat, Java, Node or database processes on Windows starting a command shell,
PowerShell, curl or a common download binary. ARTEX agents used the Windows curl binary to pull
generated scripts and post results to webhook.site.
false_positives: Line-of-business applications that call scripts. Baseline per server
name: Web or Database Service Spawns a Shell or Download Tool on Windows
query: ((process.parent.executable.caseless:(*\\w3wp.exe OR *\\httpd.exe OR *\\tomcat.exe OR *\\php\-cgi.exe OR *\\sqlservr.exe OR *\\mysqld.exe)) OR ((process.parent.executable.caseless:(*\\java.exe OR *\\node.exe)) AND (user.name:(*IIS\ APPPOOL* OR *NETWORK\ SERVICE* OR *LOCAL\ SERVICE*)))) AND (process.executable.caseless:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\bitsadmin.exe OR *\\whoami.exe OR *\\tasklist.exe))

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects a DNS lookup for _redamon-verify.<domain>, the TXT record RedAmon reads when a project turns on ownership
verification. On your resolver it means a host of yours runs RedAmon. On the name servers of your own domain it
means someone set up a RedAmon project for that domain.
false_positives: Authorized tests with RedAmon
name: RedAmon Ownership Check Lookup
query: dns.question.name:_redamon\-verify.*

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects DNS lookups for command and control domains reported in ARTEX campaigns (VAPOR PANDA
BLOODALCHEMY) and community-reported ARTEX hosting.
false_positives: Unknown
name: DNS Query for Reported ARTEX Infrastructure
query: (dns.question.name:(nginxmysql.com OR sqlserver\-sqlite.com OR www.ddduuuppp.com)) OR ((dns.question.name:(artex.lol OR artex.tokena2b.top OR artex.ok7777.eu.cc OR artex.noog2infra.site)) OR (dns.question.name:(*.artex.lol OR *.artex.tokena2b.top OR *.artex.ok7777.eu.cc OR *.artex.noog2infra.site)))

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects an AI agent client (Qwen Code, Kimi CLI, opencode, Claude Code, Codex, Pi) calling DeepSeek, Qwen on
Alibaba DashScope, GLM on BigModel or Z.ai, Kimi, MiniMax, Doubao on Volcano Engine, SiliconFlow or a model gateway such
as OpenRouter. These are the models seen behind agentic attacks (CyberStrikeAI, Cairn). Normal on some developer
machines; review it from servers, container hosts and build agents. Hunt 02 also covers consoles calling these APIs
from Go and Python.
false_positives: Developers using AI agents with these model providers
name: AI Agent Client Calling a Chinese Model API or Model Gateway
query: (user_agent.original:(QwenCode\/* OR KimiCLI\/* OR opencode\/* OR claude\-cli\/* OR codex_exec\/* OR codex_cli_rs\/* OR pi\/0.*)) AND ((url.domain:(api.deepseek.com OR dashscope.aliyuncs.com OR dashscope\-intl.aliyuncs.com OR dashscope\-us.aliyuncs.com OR open.bigmodel.cn OR api.z.ai OR api.moonshot.cn OR api.moonshot.ai OR api.kimi.com OR code.kimi.com OR api.minimax.io OR api.minimax.cn OR api.minimaxi.com OR ark.cn\-beijing.volces.com OR api.siliconflow.cn OR api.siliconflow.com OR api.stepfun.com OR tokenhub.tencentmaas.com OR qianfan.baidubce.com OR api.xiaomimimo.com OR api\-inference.modelscope.cn OR openrouter.ai OR api.novita.ai OR zenmux.ai)) OR (url.domain:(*.api.deepseek.com OR *.dashscope.aliyuncs.com OR *.dashscope\-intl.aliyuncs.com OR *.dashscope\-us.aliyuncs.com OR *.open.bigmodel.cn OR *.api.z.ai OR *.api.moonshot.cn OR *.api.moonshot.ai OR *.api.kimi.com OR *.code.kimi.com OR *.api.minimax.io OR *.api.minimax.cn OR *.api.minimaxi.com OR *.ark.cn\-beijing.volces.com OR *.api.siliconflow.cn OR *.api.siliconflow.com OR *.api.stepfun.com OR *.tokenhub.tencentmaas.com OR *.qianfan.baidubce.com OR *.api.xiaomimimo.com OR *.api\-inference.modelscope.cn OR *.openrouter.ai OR *.api.novita.ai OR *.zenmux.ai)))

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects the command CyberStrikeAI's webshell manager runs on every new webshell, "echo :OSPROBE_%OS%:END", which
shows up as a shell started by the web server process.
false_positives: Authorized tests with CyberStrikeAI
name: CyberStrikeAI Webshell OS Probe Command
query: process.command_line:*\:OSPROBE_*

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects a JSON Web Token whose header decodes to alg none, sent in a query string. ARTEX sprays the
same unsigned token across dozens of SSO paths to test for signature bypass. An alg none token has
no legitimate use against a production SSO route.
false_positives: Security scanners testing for JWT signature bypass
name: Unsigned JWT With alg none Sent to a Web Application
query: url.query:(*eyJhbGciOiJub25lI* OR *eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJub25lI* OR *eyJhbGciOiJOb25lI* OR *eyJhbGciOiJOT05FI* OR *eyJhbGciOiJub25lIiwidHlwIjoiSldUIn0.* OR *eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJub25lIn0.*)

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects a web server, application runtime or database process starting a shell, download tool or
network utility. ARTEX agents run discovery and pull tooling this way after exploiting a web
application, in quick succession and in short bursts.
false_positives: Application servers that run shell scripts by design. Baseline each service before alerting
name: Web or Database Service Spawns a Shell or Download Tool on Linux
query: (((process.parent.executable:(*\/nginx OR *\/httpd OR *\/apache2 OR *\/php\-fpm OR *\/mysqld OR *\/mariadbd OR *\/postgres)) OR process.parent.executable:*\/php\-fpm*) OR ((process.parent.executable:(*\/java OR *\/node)) AND (user.name:(www\-data OR apache OR nginx OR http OR tomcat OR tomcat9 OR jetty OR jboss OR wildfly OR node OR nodejs OR nobody OR daemon)))) AND (process.executable:(*\/sh OR *\/bash OR *\/dash OR *\/curl OR *\/wget OR *\/nc OR *\/ncat OR *\/socat OR *\/busybox))

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects an attack tool whose parent is an AI agent CLI or the shell Claude Code runs commands through
(zsh -c source ~/.claude/shell-snapshots/... on Linux and macOS, the CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL_LAUNCHER_SCRIPT PowerShell
launcher on Windows). Auto-approve flags are not part of the rule: staff use them too, and an agent can run an
attack tool without one. Qwen Code, Kimi CLI, Codex and opencode start tools through a plain shell, which puts the
agent one level above the parent, so this rule only sees them when they start the tool directly; the KQL hunt in
behaviors/sentinel/hunting covers the grandparent. The model behind the agent does not matter.
Tools written in Python, Ruby or Perl (sqlmap, NetExec, Metasploit, nikto and others) run under their interpreter,
so the image is python3, ruby or perl and the tool is the script in the command line; the script selections cover
them. A tool started as a module (python3 -m) is not covered.
Agents installed with npm or pip run under node or python and are found by their package path in the parent
command line.
false_positives: Staff who use an AI agent for authorized security testing or network troubleshooting
name: AI Agent CLI Starts an Attack Tool
query: ((process.executable:(*\/nmap OR *\\nmap.exe OR *\/naabu OR *\\naabu.exe OR *\/masscan OR *\\masscan.exe OR *\/nuclei OR *\\nuclei.exe OR *\/katana OR *\\katana.exe OR *\/dalfox OR *\\dalfox.exe OR *\/ffuf OR *\\ffuf.exe OR *\/gobuster OR *\\gobuster.exe OR *\/feroxbuster OR *\\feroxbuster.exe OR *\/sqlmap OR *\\sqlmap.exe OR *\/nikto OR *\\nikto.exe OR *\/wpscan OR *\\wpscan.exe OR *\/hydra OR *\\hydra.exe OR *\/kerbrute OR *\\kerbrute.exe OR *\/netexec OR *\\netexec.exe OR *\/nxc OR *\\nxc.exe OR *\/crackmapexec OR *\\crackmapexec.exe OR *\/bloodyAD OR *\\bloodyAD.exe OR *\/coercer OR *\\coercer.exe OR *\/chisel OR *\\chisel.exe OR *\/evil\-winrm OR *\\evil\-winrm.exe OR *\/cloudfox OR *\\cloudfox.exe OR *\/msfconsole OR *\\msfconsole.exe OR *\/dirsearch OR *\\dirsearch.exe OR *\/medusa OR *\\medusa.exe OR *\/enum4linux\-ng OR *\\enum4linux\-ng.exe OR *\/pwncat OR *\\pwncat.exe OR *\/pwncat\-cs OR *\\pwncat\-cs.exe OR *\/responder OR *\\responder.exe OR *\/searchsploit OR *\\searchsploit.exe OR *\/hashcat OR *\\hashcat.exe)) OR ((process.executable:(*\/python* OR *\\python* OR *\/ruby* OR *\\ruby* OR *\/perl* OR *\\perl*)) AND ((process.command_line:(*\/sqlmap\ * OR *\/nikto\ * OR *\/wpscan\ * OR *\/netexec\ * OR *\/nxc\ * OR *\/crackmapexec\ * OR *\/bloodyAD\ * OR *\/coercer\ * OR *\/evil\-winrm\ * OR *\/msfconsole\ * OR *\/dirsearch\ * OR *\/enum4linux\-ng\ * OR *\/pwncat\ * OR *\/pwncat\-cs\ * OR *\/responder\ * OR *\/sqlmap.py* OR *\\sqlmap.py* OR *\ sqlmap.py* OR *\/nikto.pl* OR *\\nikto.pl* OR *\ nikto.pl* OR *\/bloodyAD.py* OR *\\bloodyAD.py* OR *\ bloodyAD.py* OR *\/dirsearch.py* OR *\\dirsearch.py* OR *\ dirsearch.py* OR *\/enum4linux\-ng.py* OR *\\enum4linux\-ng.py* OR *\ enum4linux\-ng.py* OR *\/Coercer\/Coercer.py* OR *\ Coercer\/Coercer.py* OR *\\Coercer\\Coercer.py* OR *\ Coercer\\Coercer.py* OR *\/Responder\/Responder.py* OR *\ Responder\/Responder.py* OR *\\Responder\\Responder.py* OR *\ Responder\\Responder.py*)) OR (process.command_line:(*\/sqlmap OR *\/nikto OR *\/wpscan OR *\/netexec OR *\/nxc OR *\/crackmapexec OR *\/bloodyAD OR *\/coercer OR *\/evil\-winrm OR *\/msfconsole OR *\/dirsearch OR *\/enum4linux\-ng OR *\/pwncat OR *\/pwncat\-cs OR *\/responder))))) AND ((process.parent.command_line:(*shell\-snapshots* OR *CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL_LAUNCHER_SCRIPT* OR *\-\-provider\ cairn* OR *\/tmp\/cairn\-pi\/*)) OR (process.parent.executable:(*\/claude OR *\\claude.exe OR *\/codex OR *\\codex.exe OR *\/qwen OR *\\qwen.exe OR *\/kimi OR *\\kimi.exe OR *\/opencode OR *\\opencode.exe OR *\/hermes OR *\\hermes.exe)) OR (process.parent.command_line:(*@anthropic\-ai\/claude\-code* OR *@anthropic\-ai\\claude\-code* OR *@qwen\-code\/* OR *@qwen\-code\\* OR *@openai\/codex* OR *@openai\\codex* OR *opencode\-ai* OR *kimi\-cli* OR *kimi_cli*)))

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects the fixed invalid code and state values ARTEX sends to OAuth callback routes while mapping
an application.
false_positives: Unknown
name: ARTEX OAuth Callback Probe
query: url.query:*code\=AAAA\&state\=notvalidb64\!\!*

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects the pentestswarm binary or its container image, and the switches that skip its consent prompt
(PENTESTSWARM_AUTHORIZED=1, --authorized). Pentest Swarm AI runs a swarm of agents that scan and exploit a target
with no approval for each action unless assist mode is on.
false_positives: Penetration testers running Pentest Swarm AI
name: Pentest Swarm AI Started on a Host
query: (process.executable:(*\/pentestswarm OR *\\pentestswarm.exe)) OR (process.command_line:(*armur\-ai\/pentestswarm* OR *PENTESTSWARM_AUTHORIZED* OR *pentestswarm\ scan\ * OR *pentestswarm\ serve* OR *pentestswarm\-lab\-*))

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects requests whose user agent names the ARTEX agentic penetration testing framework or its
renamed builds (ScopeWeaver, AntiFox). Operators often keep the defaults. Matching is case-sensitive
in some backends, so the list carries the observed spellings.
false_positives: Authorized penetration tests that use ARTEX
name: ARTEX Agentic Attack Framework User Agent in Web Logs
query: user_agent.original:(*artex\-readonly\/* OR *artex\-pentest\/* OR *artex\-audit\/* OR *artex\-verify\/* OR *artex\-spawn\/* OR *ARTEX\-worker\/* OR *artex\-enrich\/* OR *artex\-i21861\-canary* OR *artex\-agent* OR *artex\-judge\-* OR *ARTeX\-authorized\-pentest* OR *Mozilla\/5.0\ ARTeX* OR *Mozilla\/5.0\ \(ARTEX\)* OR *ArtExVerify\/* OR *ArtEx\/1.0* OR *scopeweaver* OR *spa\-api\-recon*)

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects the files Xalgorix writes on the host that runs it: its environment files, its systemd unit, and the scan
data folder with scan.json and events.jsonl for every target.
false_positives: Bug bounty hunters and security teams running Xalgorix
name: Xalgorix Configuration, Service or Scan Data Written
query: (TargetFilename:(\/etc\/xalgorix.env OR \/etc\/systemd\/system\/xalgorix.service OR \/tmp\/xalgorix.log OR \/tmp\/xalgorix\-crash.log)) OR TargetFilename:*\/.xalgorix\/data\/* OR TargetFilename:*\/.xalgorix.env

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects the placeholder paths ARTEX agents request to learn how a site answers a missing resource,
right before a burst of guesses. These names have no legitimate caller.
false_positives: Unknown
name: ARTEX Placeholder Probe Paths
query: url.path:(*\/zzz\-nonexistent\-xyz123* OR *zzz_nonexistent_abc.txt* OR *Notexist\-xyz*)

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects the Windows persistence commands in the CyberStrikeAI implant: a Run value named SystemUpdate added with
reg.exe, or a SystemUpdate scheduled task created with schtasks. Kaspersky saw the SystemUpdate task, running as
SYSTEM and also created on remote hosts, in attacks on education organizations.
false_positives: Software that really names its updater task or Run value SystemUpdate (check the binary it starts)
name: CyberStrikeAI Implant Windows Persistence Named SystemUpdate
query: (process.command_line:*reg* AND process.command_line:*\ add\ * AND process.command_line:*\\CurrentVersion\\Run* AND process.command_line:*SystemUpdate*) OR (process.command_line:*schtasks* AND process.command_line:*\/create* AND process.command_line:*SystemUpdate*)

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects command lines that carry the names ARTEX agents give their own test artifacts: artex-probe
files with a counting number, ArtexProbe accounts, the VAPOR PANDA working folder artx5v, art18-
comments and probe marker strings.
false_positives: Authorized penetration tests that use ARTEX
name: ARTEX Artifact Names in Command Lines
query: process.command_line:(*artex\-probe\-* OR *ArtexProbe* OR *\\ProgramData\\artx5v* OR *art18\-* OR *ARTEX_WRITE_PROBE* OR *ARTX_PERSIST_OK* OR *artex_control_marker_zz9q*)

author: ThreatDefence
description: A request, sign-in or cloud API call carried a user agent that names the ARTEX framework or a renamed build.
name: ARTEX Agentic Attack Framework User Agent

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects requests from CyberStrikeAI's webshell manager to a planted webshell: its hard-coded user agent, or the
"echo :OSPROBE_%OS%:END" command it sends in the cmd parameter (visible in GET mode).
false_positives: Authorized tests with CyberStrikeAI
name: CyberStrikeAI Webshell Manager User Agent or OS Probe in Web Logs
query: user_agent.original:*CyberStrikeAI\-WebShell\/* OR (url.query:(*OSPROBE_* OR *OSPROBE%5F*))

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects requests Pentest Swarm AI sends when it maps an API or verifies a finding: the negative-control path
/nx-<16 hex> (also under /api/), the open redirect host evil.pentestswarm.invalid, the template check 191*193, and
its own user agents. All are defaults of the published code.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Pentest Swarm AI
An application with real paths named nx- and 16 hex characters
name: Pentest Swarm AI Probe Marker in Web Logs
query: (cs-method:GET AND url.path:/^\/(api\/)?nx-[0-9a-f]{16}$/) OR (url.query:(*evil.pentestswarm.invalid* OR *191\*193* OR *191%2A193*)) OR user_agent.original:pentestswarm\-*

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects the RedAmon Docker stack being run (its container names, control script and sandbox servers) and the
tunnels it opens for reverse shells: ngrok or chisel forwarding port 4444 to the Metasploit handler in its Kali
sandbox. RedAmon is a penetration testing platform; on a host that is not a tester's, find out who installed it.
false_positives: Penetration testers and students running RedAmon
Another tool that forwards port 4444 through ngrok or chisel, which is also worth a look
name: RedAmon Stack or Reverse Shell Tunnel on a Host
query: (process.command_line:(*redamon\-kali* OR *redamon\-agent* OR *redamon\-webapp* OR *redamon\-recon\-* OR *redamon\-docker\-broker* OR *\/opt\/mcp_servers\/run_servers.py* OR *\/opt\/mcp_servers\/tunnel_manager.py* OR *redamon.sh\ *)) OR process.command_line:*ngrok\ tcp\ 4444* OR (process.command_line:*chisel\ client* AND process.command_line:*R\:4444\:localhost\:4444*)

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects lookups for payload hosts that ThreatDefence saw active in ARTEX operator toolkits on November 20, 2026.
Fortinet separately reports the vietnam852.com hosts serving Gh0st RAT and an XMRig miner to brute-forced SQL Servers.
false_positives: Unknown
name: DNS Query for Payload Hosts Active in ARTEX Operator Toolkits
query: (dns.question.name:(vietnam852.com OR zhzy999.net OR jiancai008.com)) OR (dns.question.name:(*.vietnam852.com OR *.zhzy999.net OR *.jiancai008.com))

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description: Detects an MCP client driving a remote HexStrike server: requests to /api/tools/<tool> or /api/command on port 8888.
false_positives: Authorized tests with HexStrike
name: HexStrike Tool API Requested Through a Proxy
query: url.original:(*\:8888\/api\/tools\/* OR *\:8888\/api\/command*)

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description: Detects files created with the names and folders ARTEX agents use for their own test artifacts.
false_positives: Authorized penetration tests that use ARTEX
name: ARTEX Probe Artifact Created
query: TargetFilename:(*artex\-probe\-* OR *\\ProgramData\\artx5v\\* OR *zzartx0000.php*)

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description: Detects Entra ID sign-ins whose user agent names ARTEX.
false_positives: Authorized penetration tests that use ARTEX
name: ARTEX User Agent in Entra ID Sign-In Logs
query: userAgent:(*artex\-readonly\/* OR *artex\-pentest\/* OR *artex\-audit\/* OR *artex\-verify\/* OR *artex\-spawn\/* OR *ARTEX\-worker\/* OR *artex\-enrich\/* OR *artex\-i21861\-canary* OR *artex\-agent* OR *artex\-judge\-* OR *ARTeX\-authorized\-pentest* OR *Mozilla\/5.0\ ARTeX* OR *Mozilla\/5.0\ \(ARTEX\)* OR *ArtExVerify\/* OR *ArtEx\/1.0* OR *scopeweaver* OR *spa\-api\-recon*)

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects Cognito sign-up attempts that try to set custom:isAdmin or use an artex-<random>.invalid
tenant domain, as Datadog observed in ARTEX activity.
false_positives: Applications that genuinely use an isAdmin attribute in sign-up
name: Cognito Sign-Up With ARTEX Artifacts
query: (eventSource:cognito\-idp.amazonaws.com AND eventName:SignUp) AND ((errorMessage:(*custom\:isAdmin* OR *artex\-*)) OR requestParameters.userAttributes:*custom\:isAdmin*)

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects smss.exe, winlogon.exe, dllhost.exe, sihost.exe and MicrosoftEdgeUpdate.exe started from a folder
other than their real one. A toolkit active in ARTEX operations ships Gh0st RAT as winlogon.exe and an XMRig
miner as MicrosoftEdgeUpdate.exe, downloaded into user-writable folders.
false_positives: Unknown
name: Windows System Binary Name Running From the Wrong Folder
query: ((process.executable.caseless:(*\\smss.exe OR *\\winlogon.exe OR *\\dllhost.exe OR *\\sihost.exe)) AND (NOT (process.executable.caseless:(C\:\\Windows\\System32\\* OR C\:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\*)))) OR (process.executable.caseless:*\\MicrosoftEdgeUpdate.exe AND (NOT (process.executable.caseless:(*\\Microsoft\\EdgeUpdate\\* OR *\\Microsoft\\Temp\\*))))

subtechnique.name: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects creation of the JSP web shell file names Google observed when an ARTEX agent redirected the
MySQL general log into a web directory.
false_positives: Unknown
name: JSP Web Shell Names Seen in ARTEX Intrusions
query: TargetFilename:(*\/cl1217.jsp OR *\/f1219a.jsp OR *\/z1219.jsp OR *\\cl1217.jsp OR *\\f1219a.jsp OR *\\z1219.jsp)

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects the paths Xalgorix's verifier requests when it confirms a finding (<path>-xalgorix-nonexistent-<id> for
access control, xalgorix-missing-<id> before a path traversal), the reflection canary XALG0R1XTEST from its system
prompt, and its own user agents. The verifier strings are in the code; the canary is an example the model may vary.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Xalgorix
name: Xalgorix Verifier Marker or Canary in Web Logs
query: (url.path:(*xalgorix\-nonexistent\-* OR *xalgorix\-missing\-*)) OR url.query:*XALG0R1XTEST* OR user_agent.original:xalgorix*

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects lookups of the skimmer, C2 and console domains Gambit Security recovered from a financially motivated operator
who used Strix for discovery, Cairn for exploitation and Hermes for orchestration against online retailers.
false_positives: None expected
name: DNS Query for Skimmer or C2 Hosts of the Hermes, Strix and Cairn Card-Theft Campaign
query: (dns.question.name:(medbooksource.com OR traffic\-analyzer.net OR b8t.shop OR netlfjs.com OR x1opay.co OR static\-js.com OR js\-static.com OR jsnetlify.com OR netlifyjs.com OR newssjs.com)) OR (dns.question.name:(*.medbooksource.com OR *.traffic\-analyzer.net OR *.b8t.shop OR *.netlfjs.com OR *.x1opay.co OR *.static\-js.com OR *.js\-static.com OR *.jsnetlify.com OR *.netlifyjs.com OR *.newssjs.com))

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects the GameHook side-loading file names used to load the BLOODALCHEMY backdoor in the VAPOR
PANDA ARTEX campaign, outside a legitimate game install.
false_positives: Legitimate GameHook or OBS installations
name: BLOODALCHEMY Loader Files Written
query: file.path:(*\\graphics\-hook\-filter64.dll OR *\\graphics\-hook_config.bin)

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description: Detects AWS API calls whose user agent names ARTEX.
false_positives: Authorized penetration tests that use ARTEX
name: ARTEX User Agent in AWS CloudTrail
query: userAgent:(*artex\-readonly\/* OR *artex\-pentest\/* OR *artex\-audit\/* OR *artex\-verify\/* OR *artex\-spawn\/* OR *ARTEX\-worker\/* OR *artex\-enrich\/* OR *artex\-i21861\-canary* OR *artex\-agent* OR *artex\-judge\-* OR *ARTeX\-authorized\-pentest* OR *Mozilla\/5.0\ ARTeX* OR *Mozilla\/5.0\ \(ARTEX\)* OR *ArtExVerify\/* OR *ArtEx\/1.0* OR *scopeweaver* OR *spa\-api\-recon*)

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects svchost.exe started from any folder other than System32 or SysWOW64. In the VAPOR PANDA
campaign a renamed GameHook binary named svchost.exe side-loaded the BLOODALCHEMY backdoor.
false_positives: Unknown
name: Svchost Running Outside the Windows System Folder
query: process.executable.caseless:*\\svchost.exe AND (NOT (process.executable.caseless:(C\:\\Windows\\System32\\* OR C\:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\* OR C\:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\*)))

subtechnique.name: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects the shell wrapper PentAGI puts around every agent command in its Kali worker container: it ignores hangups,
raises the process's oom_score_adj by one to mark the flow, then runs the command with exec sh -c "$0".
false_positives: Authorized red team use of PentAGI
name: PentAGI Agent Command Wrapper
query: process.command_line:*trap\ \"\"\ HUP* AND process.command_line:*\/proc\/self\/oom_score_adj* AND process.command_line:*exec\ sh\ \-c\ \"$0\"*

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects the Strix CLI starting a scan, the strix-agent package being installed, the ghcr.io/usestrix/strix-sandbox
container being run, or the Caido proxy the sandbox starts with guest access.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Strix
name: Strix AI Pentest Agent CLI or Sandbox
query: process.command_line:/(^|[\/\\\s])strix(\.exe)?["']?\s(.*\s)?(--target|-t|--target-list|--scan-mode|--resume)[\s=]/ OR process.command_line:/((pip|pip3|pipx)\s+install|uv\s+(tool\s+install|tool\s+run|pip\s+install)|uvx)\s(.*\s)?[\"']?strix-agent/ OR process.command_line:*usestrix\/strix\-sandbox* OR (process.command_line:*caido\-cli* AND process.command_line:*\-\-allow\-guests*)

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects Strix's telemetry calls (POST /scan_started/, /finding_reported/ and /scan_ended/ on strix.gateway.scarf.sh)
and requests to the Strix results viewer's agent steering API.
false_positives: Authorized tests with Strix
name: Strix Telemetry or Results Viewer API in Proxy Logs
query: (url.domain:(strix.gateway.scarf.sh OR *.strix.gateway.scarf.sh)) OR url.original:*\/api\/agents\/steer*

author: T, h, r, e, a, t, D, e, f, e, n, c, e
description:
Detects CyberStrikeAI traffic leaving your network: the console's own user agents (CyberStrikeAI/<version> to
internet search APIs and chat bots, CyberStrikeAI-WebShell/ to webshells) and the implant's default user agent, a
Chrome string cut short after AppleWebKit/537.36 that no browser sends, matched exactly.
false_positives: Authorized tests with CyberStrikeAI
Scripts that copy the same truncated user agent (implant selection only)
name: CyberStrikeAI User Agents or Implant Check-in in Proxy Logs
query: (user_agent.original:(CyberStrikeAI\/* OR CyberStrikeAI\-Docker\-build*)) OR user_agent.original:*CyberStrikeAI\-WebShell\/* OR user_agent.original:"Mozilla\/5.0 \(Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64\) AppleWebKit\/537.36"

author: ThreatDefence
description: Ten or more EC2 calls with the DryRun flag from one identity in five minutes, the capability check ARTEX agents run with a stolen AWS key.
name: Burst of EC2 DryRun Calls From One Identity
query:
from logs-aws.cloudtrail-*
| where aws.cloudtrail.error_code == "Client.DryRunOperation"
| stats dryruns = count(*), actions = count_distinct(event.action) by aws.cloudtrail.user_identity.arn, source.ip
| where dryruns >= 10
